title: Full mixed grid + 2–3 syllable combinations + checkpoint dry run
objectives: Student can read any cell of the full 84-cell grid (28 letters × 3 harakat) on sight, fully randomized, with zero major (Jali-tier) errors.
Student can decode 2–3 syllable combinations built from familiar letters and all 3 harakat, including combinations not seen before (a genuine transfer/fluency test).
Student and teacher jointly know, going into Checkpoint 1, exactly which specific letters/sounds remain weak (Khafi-tier) so revision time isn't wasted on already-solid material.

slides.heading: Lesson 1.12 — Full mixed grid + syllables + checkpoint dry run

audio.cue: ا: an open, unobstructed sound from deep in the chest cavity — no closure anywhere, just a clear open vowel
lips fully together
tongue-tip on gum ridge
tongue between teeth
ح: a strong, breathy, unvoiced friction from the middle of the throat — like fogging a mirror from deep in the throat, no English equivalent
خ: a rasping fricative from the upper throat/back of the tongue against the soft palate — a genuine back-of-throat 'kh', not softened
د: tongue-tip taps the upper gum ridge firmly — a plain, crisp 'd'
ذ: tongue-tip between the teeth, same point as ث but VOICED — 'th' as in 'this', never a 'z'

audio.title: Arabic101 Makharij Lesson 10 — ر (ra), the ULTIMATE guide

audio.cue: ز: tip of tongue near the lower teeth, a plain buzzing 'z' — voiced twin of س
س: tip of tongue near the lower teeth, a thin hiss — a plain 's'
ش: middle of tongue against the roof of the mouth, a soft 'sh'
ع: a mid-throat muscular squeeze, voiced — no equivalent sound in English or Turkic languages
غ: upper throat, same zone as خ but voiced — a uvular fricative, like a French uvular 'r'
ف: inner lower lip against the edge of the upper front teeth — a plain 'f'
ك: back of tongue against the soft palate, shallower in the mouth than ق — a plain 'k'
م: the two lips, with nasal resonance — 'm'
ه: a light, breathy throat release — a soft 'h', much gentler than ح
و: rounded lips — a consonant 'w'
ي: middle of tongue toward the roof of the mouth — a consonant 'y'

slides.heading: Mock Checkpoint 1 run-through
body: Teacher runs the actual Checkpoint 1 test script, live, treating it as a rehearsal — logs results on the real rubric sheet.
This mirrors the qaida tradition's own consolidation step, so the real checkpoint feels familiar rather than high-stakes-novel.

slides.heading: Joint debrief
body: Teacher and student review the rubric sheet together.
Agree on which 1–2 areas (if any) need a few extra days of home practice before the real checkpoint.

slides.heading: What to expect at the real Checkpoint 1
body: Same test script you just rehearsed: warm-up recognition pass, makhraj (where the sound is born in your mouth or throat) spot-check, positional reading, vowel grid spot-check, syllable transfer test, wrap-up.
A failed checkpoint never means restarting Phase 1 — it triggers targeted revision of only the specific weak unit(s), then a retest.

slides.heading: Homework — 15–20 min/day
tasks: In your notebook, write today's marked syllables (بَتَ، سَرَ، مَنَ، كَتَبَ، دَرَسَ، سَمِعَ …) 4 full rows, saying each syllable aloud as you write, then memorize them
Full 84-cell grid, randomized self-quiz, daily — this also reviews every letter learned so far
Re-read all syllable combinations (2- and 3-syllable) from today, 3× through
Focused extra practice only on whatever 1–2 specific weak spots the joint debrief identified — not a blanket repeat of everything
Rest/consolidate the day immediately before the real Checkpoint 1 session (light review only, no new drilling)

dailyChecklist: Write today's marked syllables 4 rows each in your notebook, saying each syllable aloud as you write
Re-read all syllable combinations (2- and 3-syllable) from today, 3× through
Focused extra practice only on whatever 1–2 specific weak spots the joint debrief identified
Rest/consolidate the day immediately before the real Checkpoint 1 session (light review only, no new drilling)

script: Open with the full 28-letter shuffle as a baseline confidence check before revealing the 84-cell mixed grid.

Since no vetted 'hear the whole grid' video is wired in for this course yet (candidates remain unverified/audition-required per verified-resources.md §4), demonstrate the full 84-cell interleaved grid live yourself before the four guided quarters.
Run all four guided quarters (21 cells each) before introducing any syllable combinations — full-grid fluency first, then multi-cell decoding.
Introduce 2-syllable combinations before 3-syllable ones, then the cold-read transfer set — the cold-read items are the one genuinely unseen-material check, so observe without prompting.
Run the actual Checkpoint 1 test script live as a rehearsal, logging results on the real rubric sheet, exactly as the real checkpoint will be scored.
Close with the joint debrief — name the 1–2 specific weak spots together with the student, never a vague 'you're basically ready.'
listenFor: Full re-check of every item on the high-risk watchlist accumulated across Phase 1: ح/خ/ه confusion, ص/ض/ط/ظ tafkheem, ع vs ء, غ vs خ vs ق, ق vs ك, ذ/ز/ض "D→Z" collapse pattern, ر tongue-tap quality, fatha/kasra/damma timing (no lengthening into madd).

During the mock checkpoint run-through specifically: distinguish Jali (wrong letter/sound entirely — hard-fail signal) from Khafi (right letter/sound but quality slightly off — flag-and-practice signal), using the rubric in the Checkpoint 1 Kit, so the debrief conversation is concrete rather than vague ("you're basically ready" vs. "here are the 3 specific cells to drill").
Syllable-transfer set specifically: does the student sound out letter-by-letter still, or read the combination fluently? Either is fine at this stage, but note it for Phase 2 pacing.
teacherNotes.homework: In the student's notebook: today's marked syllables written 4 full rows, saying each aloud while writing, then memorized. Full 84-cell grid, randomized self-quiz, daily (also reviews every letter learned so far). Re-read all syllable combinations (2- and 3-syllable) from today, 3× through. Focused extra practice only on whatever 1–2 specific weak spots the joint debrief identified — not a blanket repeat of everything. Rest/consolidate the day immediately before the real Checkpoint 1 session (light review only, no new drilling). No printed sheets.
